# Results — Study 922 (Floating-Rate Front End) on the real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Four front-end sleeves are
held, not traded: the two Treasury floating-rate-note funds **USFR** and **TFLO** (coupons
reset weekly off the 13-week bill auction, ~0 duration), the T-bill fund **BIL**, and the
1-3 year fixed-coupon fund **SHY** (~1.85 years of duration). Daily **total-return** closes
(`yfinance`, `auto_adjust=True`); **^IRX**, the 13-week bill discount rate, is a
**price-only yield index** and is never held — it supplies the regime label and the cash
accrual proxy. Common window 2014-02-04 → 2026-06-30 (USFR/TFLO inception gates it).
As-of **2026-06-30** (the partial current month is dropped).*

## Data stamp

| Legs | Window | n days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| USFR, TFLO, BIL, SHY (total return) + ^IRX (yield index) | 2014-02-04 → 2026-06-30 | 3,118 | `4bfc2a85745c` (`quantlab.repro`), raw-array `c7727a818f38` |

**Survivorship:** none, and it is worth naming. There is no cross-section here — these are
four named, still-listed funds chosen ex ante as *the* liquid instruments for the job, so
no dead fund has been quietly dropped. The bias that does exist is a **launch-liquidity**
one, cut out explicitly below.

## The four sleeves

Excess-of-cash uses the ^IRX/252 accrual **proxy** (see the caveat under *Cash proxy*).

| Fund | Total return | Vol | Max drawdown | Excess-of-cash | Excess Sharpe (HAC *t*) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **USFR** (floater) | +1.91%/yr | 1.46% | −2.12% | +0.029%/yr | +0.02 (*t* = +0.12) |
| **TFLO** (floater) | +1.95%/yr | 1.98% | −5.01% | +0.067%/yr | +0.03 (*t* = +0.33) |
| **BIL** (bills) | +1.75%/yr | 0.26% | −0.24% | −0.131%/yr | −0.56 (*t* = −4.24) |
| **SHY** (1-3y fixed) | +1.48%/yr | 1.47% | −5.71% | −0.406%/yr | −0.28 (*t* = −1.04) |

Over twelve and a half years spanning a full cycle, **the floaters paid the most and the
1-3 year fixed leg paid the least** — but the gaps are tens of basis points and the vol of
the floaters' *quoted* returns is inflated by their illiquid first years (below).

## The pairwise race — annualised difference and HAC *t*

| Pair | Difference | HAC *t* | Tracking vol | Days a wins |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| USFR − BIL | **+0.160%/yr** | +0.68 | 1.47% | 40.3% |
| TFLO − BIL | **+0.198%/yr** | +0.96 | 1.98% | 42.5% |
| USFR − SHY | **+0.435%/yr** | +0.96 | 2.07% | 48.9% |
| TFLO − SHY | +0.473%/yr | +1.07 | 2.44% | 48.9% |
| BIL − SHY | +0.275%/yr | +0.72 | 1.46% | 47.9% |
| USFR − TFLO | −0.038%/yr | −0.13 | 2.69% | 42.8% |

**No unconditional pair clears |*t*| = 2.** Every sign points the same way — floaters ≥
bills ≥ 1-3y fixed — and the two floaters are indistinguishable from each other, but on
the full tape the differences are inside the noise. The "days a wins" column below 50% next
to a positive mean is the signature of an income vehicle: it wins small and often on
accrual days and loses on the days its NAV is marked.

## Liquidity-era cut

USFR and TFLO launched in February 2014 and traded by appointment for years: USFR's quoted
vol was **2.7% annualised in 2014** against **0.28% in 2025**, and TFLO printed a +466 bp
day followed by a −446 bp day in December 2014. Those are quote artefacts an order of
magnitude larger than the economics under test.

| Era | USFR − BIL | TFLO − BIL | USFR − SHY |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2014-2017 (launch, illiquid) | +0.169% (*t* = +0.23) | +0.317% (*t* = +0.44) | −0.126% (*t* = −0.16) |
| 2018-2026 (liquid) | +0.155% (*t* = +1.40) | **+0.143% (*t* = +2.08)** | +0.693% (*t* = +1.24) |

The *point estimate* of the floater-over-bills pickup is stable across eras (≈ +15 bps/yr,
which is what a Treasury FRN's discount margin net of a 15 bp fee should be); only the
noise shrinks. One of the four era/fund cells clears *t* = 2 — a single cell out of many is
not a robust rejection of zero, and we do not treat it as one.

## Regime cut on the direction of ^IRX

Label: the sign of the 63-day change in the 13-week bill rate through day *t*, dead band
±0.25 pp, **applied to day *t*+1** — the study's single execution lag.

| Regime | n | USFR | BIL | SHY | USFR − SHY | USFR − BIL |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **rising** | 626 | +2.65% | +2.12% | **−0.04%** | **+2.69%** (*t* = +1.94) | +0.53% (*t* = +1.26) |
| flat | 2,038 | +1.55% | +1.49% | +1.73% | −0.18% (*t* = −0.35) | +0.05% (*t* = +0.14) |
| falling | 390 | +3.14% | +2.84% | +2.87% | +0.26% (*t* = +0.23) | +0.30% (*t* = +1.15) |

## Headline test — does the direction of rates flip the ranking?

One HAC-OLS regression per pair on the *whole* sample (daily difference, in annualised pp,
on rising- and falling-rate dummies), so this is one test rather than a walk through
sub-samples. The **contrast** is the floater's advantage when rates rise minus its
advantage when they fall — literally the difference of the two columns beside it, with its
HAC standard error taken from the full covariance matrix of the fit.

| Pair | Flat | Rising extra | Falling extra | **Contrast** |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| USFR − SHY | −0.18% (*t* = −0.35) | +2.87 (*t* = +1.92) | +0.45 (*t* = +0.37) | **+2.43 pp/yr (*t* = +1.37)** |
| BIL − SHY | −0.23% (*t* = −0.62) | +2.39 (*t* = +1.76) | +0.20 (*t* = +0.18) | +2.19 pp/yr (*t* = +1.33) |
| USFR − BIL | +0.05% (*t* = +0.15) | +0.48 (*t* = +0.82) | +0.25 (*t* = +0.57) | +0.23 pp/yr (*t* = +0.48) |

The direction of the effect is exactly what duration arithmetic predicts, and it is large —
~2.4 pp/yr of swing on the floater-vs-fixed choice — but **it does not clear *t* = 2**. One
tightening cycle is one observation, however many days it contains.

*Estimator note (audit fix).* An earlier build read this contrast off a **restricted**
regression on a single ``rising − falling`` regressor. That specification quietly borrows
the 2,038 flat days to pin the midpoint between the two groups, and on an unbalanced split
(626 rising vs 390 falling days) it returned **+2.95 pp/yr (*t* = +1.56)** — a number 22%
larger than the rising-minus-falling gap it was captioned as, and visibly inconsistent with
the +2.87 / +0.45 columns printed next to it. The contrast is now the unrestricted linear
combination, so the table is internally consistent and the headline is smaller.

**Classifier sweep** (12 window/dead-band combinations): the contrast is **positive in
12/12**, ranging +0.03 to +6.41 pp/yr, with |*t*| ≥ 2 in **0/12** (the closest is the
63-day / 0.10 pp setting at +2.69, *t* = +1.94). Robust in sign, never significant in any
setting. Two of the twelve settings are effectively zero (+0.03 at 63/0.50, +1.15 at
126/0.10), so "robust in sign" should be read as *never negative*, not as *stable in size*.

## The rate cycle, window by window (declared ASSUMPTION: a hardcoded Fed calendar)

| Window | n | USFR | TFLO | BIL | SHY | USFR − SHY | USFR − BIL |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| ZIRP + first hikes 2014-02→2021-12 | 1,991 | +0.73% | +0.76% | +0.58% | **+1.11%** | −0.38% (*t* = −0.80) | +0.15% (*t* = +0.39) |
| hiking 2022-03→2023-07 | 356 | +3.39% | +3.32% | +2.85% | **−1.07%** | **+4.46%** (*t* = +1.99) | **+0.54%** (*t* = +2.05) |
| plateau 2023-08→2024-08 | 274 | +4.83% | +5.22% | +5.24% | **+5.50%** | −0.66% (*t* = −0.40) | −0.40% (*t* = −0.89) |
| cutting 2024-09→2026-06 | 457 | +4.24% | +4.22% | +4.07% | +3.39% | +0.86% (*t* = +0.87) | +0.17% (*t* = +1.26) |

Two of the four windows favour the fixed leg, two favour the floater. The hiking window is
where the floater earns its reputation — and it is also the only window where either
comparison touches *t* = 2, on 356 days.

## What the FRN gives up when rates fall

Less than the textbook says, so far. The floater's cost is the **term premium** it declines
to collect, and this tape prices that at roughly **0.4-0.7 pp/yr**: SHY out-earned USFR by
0.38 pp/yr through the ZIRP era and by 0.66 pp/yr through the plateau. The big prize —
duration's capital gain in a cutting cycle — **has not shown up**: through 2024-09 → 2026-06
the floater still beat SHY by +0.86 pp/yr, because the curve stayed flat-to-inverted (the
1-3y yield fell far less than the 13-week rate) and cuts came slowly.

| Window | Δ^IRX | USFR cum | SHY cum | Realised gap | Predicted D×Δy (D = 1.60 / 1.85 / 2.10) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| ZIRP + first hikes | −0.02 pp | +5.80% | +9.16% | **−3.36%** | −0.04 / −0.04 / −0.05 |
| hiking | +4.94 pp | +4.91% | −1.55% | **+6.45%** | +7.90 / +9.13 / +10.36 |
| plateau | −0.29 pp | +5.39% | +6.14% | −0.74% | −0.47 / −0.54 / −0.61 |
| cutting | −1.24 pp | +8.00% | +6.31% | **+1.68%** | −1.98 / −2.29 / −2.60 |

Duration explains the sign and order of magnitude in the hiking window (+6.45% realised vs
+9.13% predicted — the gap is the curve inverting, so the 1-3y yield rose less than the bill
rate). It gets the **cutting window wrong by 4 pp**, and misses the ZIRP era entirely, where
the floater's shortfall is carry, not price. The effective duration is an assumption swept
1.60-2.10 and none of that changes.

## Drawdowns (absolute, lived)

| Fund | Max DD, full | Vol, full | Max DD, 2018+ | Vol, 2018+ |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| USFR | −2.12% | 1.46% | **−0.40%** | 0.60% |
| TFLO | −5.01% | 1.98% | **−0.16%** | 0.41% |
| BIL | −0.24% | 0.26% | −0.21% | 0.24% |
| SHY | −5.71% | 1.47% | **−5.71%** | 1.67% |

This is the sharpest number in the study and it is a *risk* number, not a return one. In
the liquid era the floaters' worst loss is **0.2-0.4%** against SHY's **−5.7%** (October
2022) — the same total return for a fourteenth of the drawdown. The floaters' ugly
full-sample drawdowns (−2.1%, −5.0%) are entirely 2014-2015 quote artefacts.

| Pair | Point | 95% CI | share < 0 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| USFR − BIL | +0.160%/yr | [−0.244, +0.548] | 21.4% |
| USFR − SHY | +0.435%/yr | [−0.432, +1.321] | 15.0% |

Every interval straddles zero.

## Costs, borrow and the cash proxy

- **Cost (held sleeve).** Choosing one sleeve over another is a round trip on each leg, once
  — not a daily trade. At a 1 bp spread the USFR−SHY difference goes +0.435% → **+0.395%**
  over a one-year hold and **+0.421%** over three years; at a punitive 5 bps, +0.235% /
  +0.368%. **Friction does not decide this study** — the noise does.
- **Borrow (long/short pair).** Read as a dollar-neutral pair, the same difference dies at
  a plausible fee: +0.435% gross → +0.185% at 25 bps → **−0.065% at 50 bps** → −0.565% at
  100 bps. There is no pair trade here.
- **Cash proxy.** The pairwise differences are invariant to the cash convention (cash
  cancels). The *individual* excess Sharpes are not: BIL's excess Sharpe is −0.56 on an
  ^IRX/252 accrual and **+1.84** on ^IRX/360, because a level shift of a few bps dominates a
  series with 0.26% vol. That fragility is exactly why the headline of this study is the
  **pairwise difference**, not an excess Sharpe league table.

## Synthetic control (machinery proof only — never supports the stamp)

On a planted front-end panel where the fixed leg carries 1.85 years of duration, the same
regime estimator returns a contrast of **+8.35 pp/yr (*t* = +14.2)** — floater +5.43 pp/yr
extra when rates rise, −2.92 pp/yr when they fall, exactly the planted flip (and note that
+5.43 − (−2.92) = +8.35: the corrected estimator reproduces its own columns). On the null,
where the rate cycle is identical but the "fixed" leg has **no duration**, the contrast is
centred at **+0.14 pp/yr (sd 0.40)** and fires |*t*| ≥ 2 on **0/8** seeds. The estimator
recovers a real flip and stays quiet without one, so the real-tape *t* = 1.37 is a fact
about a twelve-year sample containing one hiking cycle, not a broken harness.

## Verdict

- **Signal — Weak.** The economics are visible and correctly signed everywhere: floaters
  beat 1-3y fixed by **+4.46 pp/yr** through the 2022-2023 hikes and lose to it by
  0.4-0.7 pp/yr when rates sit still, and the rising-minus-falling contrast is **positive in
  12/12** classifier settings. But **nothing clears a robust |*t*| = 2**: the headline
  contrast is +2.43 pp/yr at *t* = +1.37 and clears 2 in **0/12** classifier settings, the
  unconditional USFR−BIL and USFR−SHY differences are *t* = +0.68 and +0.96 with bootstrap
  CIs straddling zero, and the two cells that do touch 2 (the 356-day hiking window;
  TFLO−BIL post-2018) are single cells among many. *This stamp was **Mixed** in the first
  build and was cut to **Weak** in audit, for two reasons.* First, correcting the contrast
  estimator (above) took the headline from *t* = +1.56 and 1/12 settings clearing 2 to
  *t* = +1.37 and **0/12** — there is now no setting, cut or window that certifies the
  effect. Second, the house rule reserves `MIXED` for a verdict that splits into *stamps*
  by regime ("Real on the level · None on the spike"); here no regime earns `REAL`, so the
  split is between *insignificant-positive* and *insignificant-negative*, which is a
  textbook mechanism the tape cannot certify — the definition of `WEAK`. The sign is not in
  doubt; the size is entirely inside the noise of one hiking cycle.
- **Tradability — Fragile.** What is bankable is thin and conditional. The floater-over-bills
  pickup is ≈ **+15 bps/yr** — genuinely there in both eras and untouched by cost, but the
  size of a fee decision, not an edge. The floater-over-1-3y choice pays **only if you know
  which way rates are going**, which is the whole problem; as a dollar-neutral pair it is
  negative past 50 bps of borrow. The one durable, costless improvement is a **risk** one:
  in the liquid era the floaters delivered SHY's return with a −0.4% worst drawdown against
  −5.7%. That is a duration decision an investor can make deliberately, not an alpha.
- **Which end of the cash curve pays more?** On this tape, the floating end — by a nose, and
  mostly because it was the end you wanted to own in one 17-month stretch. The 1-3 year fixed
  end has yet to be paid back for that in the cutting cycle it was supposed to win.
